To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
consumption of highly CAF diet induces anxiolytic and antidepressant behaviors in mice, and that these changes are related to BDNF and GDNF levels in the hippocampus.
consumption of palatable diet induces an antidepressant- and anti-anxiety-like behaviors and increases BDNF and nerve growth factor expression in mice.
consumption of palatable cafeteria diets induces antidepressant- or anxiolytic behaviors, which are related to BDNF and/or NGF expression increases.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of CAF on behaviors and neurotrophins levels in mice, which could help to understand the mechanisms involved in the development of mood and anxiety disorders in humans.
the impact of the consumption of palatible high-fat and high- sugar foods on cognitive and non-cognitive behaviors and brain factors in mice.
the impact of CAF intake on cognitive and behavioral alterations in mice, as well as on brain neurotrophic factors’ levels.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the CAF diet induces anxiolytic and antidepressant-like behaviors, which could be related to the BDNF and GDNF protein expression in the hippocampus.
the consumption of highly palatable food can be related with the expression of BDNF and/or NGF in hippocampus of CAF group.
the CAF group exhibited antidepressant- and anxiety-like effects that could be associated with the increase of BDNF and GDNF in hippocampus of these mice.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the CAF diet has an antidepressant- and anxiety-like effect in the mice.
the consumption of CAF diet in the present study was associated with a decrease in the depressive-like and anxiety-like behaviors and increase in the expression of hippocampal BDNF and GDNF in mice.
the consumption of highly palatable foods induces changes in the neurobiological pathways that regulate behaviors.
The main takeaway from our work is that

palatable CAF consumption induces antidepressant- and anxiolytic- like behaviors and increases BDNF and NGF levels in hippocampus, which could be related to the improvement of mood in mice from the CDF group.
a diet high in fat and sugar can improve depressive-like and anxiety-like behaviors in mice, and this may be due to increased expression of brain neurotrophin factors.
palatable CAF diet can induce antidepressant- and antianxiety-like effects and increase BDNF and GDNF protein levels in hippocampus.
